findings.title: Aligns with the maintenance initiative's scope and guidelines
findings.description: This is a non-trivial, cross-cutting bug fix (review truncation + model identity) that fits the 900 architecture's "bug fixes / operational logging" scope and its "small, focused, independently deliverable" guidance. The design repeatedly resists scope growth — deferring diff ordering/`--stat` (#137), file-body truncation (#138), default changes, and speculative threshold gates — and has no dependencies. Effort (3/5) and mechanism count (two small pure helpers plus metadata stamping) are proportionate to the three plan-assigned parts.

findings.title: CLI and pipeline parity is structural, not duplicated
findings.description: I confirmed both `cli/commands/review.py::_execute_review` and `pipeline/actions/review.py::_review` call `run_review_with_profile`, and both then persist via `save_review_result` → `format_review_markdown`. Placing the diff stamp, model stamp, and `impose_diff_coverage` inside `run_review_with_profile` (after telemetry assignment and after the #92 recovery turn, as Special Considerations requires) means the new facts ride one `ReviewResult` to frontmatter, header, JSON, terminal, and `ActionResult`. The `verdictSource=imposed` addition needs no gate change (confirmed: the COMMIT review-verdict gate validates `verdict` against `Verdict` only, and `CONCERNS` is a valid member), and `CheckpointTrigger.ON_CONCERNS` will trip on the imposed verdict on the pipeline path.

findings.title: Synthetic coverage finding omits the required location token
findings.description: The design states the synthetic finding "has no `location` because it cites no file." That decision conflicts with the established finding contract from slice 904 and project conventions: every finding carries a `location:`, with `unverified` (`UNVERIFIED_LOCATION` in `parsers.py`) as the explicit token when there is no file. Because the synthetic `ReviewFinding` is constructed directly rather than parsed, it never passes through `_normalize_location`, so `structured_findings` maps `f.location or f.file_ref` → `None` and persistence omits the `location` line entirely; `to_dict()` emits `"location": None`. This makes the coverage finding the first artifact finding with no location at all, inconsistent with every other finding and with consumers that read location (ensemble dedup per 904 keys on it; metrology `_canonical_projection` reads `location`). Set the synthetic finding's `location` to `UNVERIFIED_LOCATION` with `location_verified=None` to keep the artifact schema consistent.

findings.title: Walkthrough step 6 cannot exercise multiple profiles, leaving D9's false-positive mitigation unverified
findings.description: Step 6 says to run "one per configured profile (sdk, openai, openrouter, local)" but the command is hardcoded to `sq review slice 927 --model sonnet -v`. In `cli/commands/review.py::_resolve_model_and_profile`, a model flag with no `--profile` resolves the profile from the alias (`alias_profile`); `sonnet` resolves to one provider. So the identical command four times captures the same alias's model id, not the openai/openrouter/local id forms that D9's equivalence rule must tolerate. This is the only planned defense for the risk named in Risk Assessment ("D9 false positives on a live router… dropped `vendor/` prefix or a `:free` suffix"), and Mitigation Strategies (line 363) explicitly relies on step 6 to "capture each profile's real ids before merge." As written, the mitigation cannot fire and the false-positive risk retires unverified. The step should vary `--profile` with a model valid for each profile, and record the observed id for each.

findings.title: The headline "PASS means saw the whole diff or read files" is a plan-sanctioned heuristic, not a guarantee
findings.description: Part B fires only when `tool_calls_made - failed_tool_calls == 0`; any single successful tool call suppresses the cap regardless of whether that call read the omitted portion of the diff. The slice plan explicitly accepts "a truncated diff where the model did read files stays a normal verdict," so this is a deliberate proxy rather than a gap — but the Value statement is stronger than the mechanism ("a PASS means the model either saw the whole diff or read files with its tools"). Worth keeping the wording honest in the artifact/CHANGELOG so downstream gate owners do not read the cap as a guarantee that the omitted bytes were reviewed.

structured_findings.summary: Aligns with the maintenance initiative's scope and guidelines
CLI and pipeline parity is structural, not duplicated
Synthetic coverage finding omits the required location token
Walkthrough step 6 cannot exercise multiple profiles, leaving D9's false-positive mitigation unverified
The headline "PASS means saw the whole diff or read files" is a plan-sanctioned heuristic, not a guarantee
